contexts.text: The sun was setting () = the state before consummation.
The setting of the sun is the last time of the Church, called consummation.
The sun had set () = the last time, when there is consummation. AE 539:3.
The setting of the sun, etc. = falsities and evils.
The sun had set () = life in what is obscure. Explained.

The setting of the sun = falsity and evil in which are those with whom there are no charity and faith; thus also the last time of the Church; and it also = what is obscure as to the things of good and truth... Illustrated.

The Lord sets with everyone who does not receive truth and good. Not that the Sun there sets... but he who does not receive it causes it to as it were set with himself. (So the natural sun) does not set... Thus the setting is not in the sun.
The sun shall set at noon () = that the good of celestial love would recede.
Until the setting of the sun () = when that state ceased. Explained.
The sun neither rises nor sets... (So) the Sun of Heaven is said to set, when man is in evil and thence in falsity... The Lord is always in the rising... and never in the setting.
The entering, or setting, of the sun = a state of shade from the delights of external loves.
The setting of the Sun in Heaven corresponds to a state of shade as to the truths of faith, and to a state of cold as to the good of love...
Its setting = good from Him in obscure perception.
They sacrificed the Passover when the sun had set, because the setting of the sun = the last time of the Church.
The setting of the sun = the evil of love, which is the evil of life. Illustrated.
The setting of the sun also = the state of the Church when it is in ignorance, which is its first state. It also = the state of the Church when it is in evils and falsities. Illustrated.
From the rising and from the setting = all in the goods and truths of the Church. Illustrated.
The setting () = the end of the Church.
Her sun has set while it is as yet day () = to perish as to all goods of love.
